thread:
sam_infra: quick heads-up — after the overnight smoke runs in eu-south we saw a spike in failed GPU attaches (~5%) tied to nodes with high local-nvme write latency. trace looks like janitor cleanup + batch teardown hitting the same disks. iostat showed write_qdepth bouncing.
anya_sre: ugh. any pattern on which instance types or pools?
sam_infra: mostly g5-smallish nodes in pool `batch-eu-south-2`. SMART shows increased write amp on a subset, but not full device failures. suspect cleanup concurrency.
ben_storage: can you paste the `iostat -x` snapshot and the janitor job schedule? curious about overlapping fstrim / scrub windows.
sam_infra: pasted logs:

```
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1        12.0   420.5  1024.0  81920.0   196.0   21.3    42.1   1.9   44.2   0.9  89.4
```

and janitor cron: `0 */2 * * * /opt/cleaner/run --batch-size=500 --concurrency=8`
kai_ml: 8 concurrent cleaners per node seems high for these drives. write amplification + small-block churn will push qdepth.
lina_ops: rolling patch landed last week bumped cleaner concurrency default to 8 (was 3) — this matches the timing.
anya_sre: okay quick mitigation options: revert cleaner concurrency, throttle via cpulimit, or move scrub window. which is fastest?
ben_storage: reverting concurrency to 3 is lowest-risk. also we can set a temporary per-node io scheduler knob: `echo 32 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests` to cap outstanding requests.
sam_infra: i can roll revert in eu-south canary first. will also add a temporary rate-limit in the cleaner config and sticky label to avoid scheduling batch teardown at same time.
deploy-bot: deploy started: cleaner-config@eu-south canary (commit sha: a1b2c3d) — ETA 4m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
anya_sre: monitoring dash up — watch %util and attach failures. notify @oncall if attach rate > 2% for 15m.
lina_ops: kicked off canary revert, 12 nodes updated so far. so far %util dropping from ~88% -> ~52% on updated hosts.
kai_ml: does this affect throughput for normal workloads? we should measure tail latency for small requests too.
ben_storage: agreed but for now availability > marginal perf. we can later tune concurrency by disk model via telemetry.
sam_infra: post-mitigation note: will open runbook PR with recommended defaults and a small telemetry flag: `nvme.cleaner.concurrency` per sku. also adding a permanent constraint to avoid cleaner + batch-teardown overlap.
anya_sre: thanks. assign follow-up to @ben_storage for telemetry + sku defaults, @lina_ops for config rollback bake + runbook, @sam_infra for postmortem draft if this reappears.
sam_infra: noted. i'll post a short postmortem if we see regression after revert.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: cleaner-config@eu-south canary — all checks passed :white_check_mark:
lina_ops: can we tag the affected nodes for healthscan and schedule deeper SMART checks tomorrow morning? i'll do that.
ben_storage: added task, will aggregate wear metrics and produce a short CSV by EOD.
kai_ml: thanks all. good catch — lucky the canary surfaced it.
anya_sre: closing loop: if attach failures stay <1% for 2h we can promote revert cluster-wide. else rollback plan B (throttle janitor at infra level).
sam_infra: promoting in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:
